Three delegated generations. (1) token-shunt:code-writer --worker-model auto --reference {FIX}/gen/verify/config_ref.json --target {TMP}/vl_config.json --verify "jq empty {TMP}/vl_config.json" --spec "config_ref に沿った JSON。必須キー required_key を含む". (2) token-shunt:code-writer --worker-model auto --reference {FIX}/gen/verify/notes_ref.md --target {TMP}/vl_notes.md --spec "notes_ref に沿った 30 行の Markdown". (3) token-shunt:code-writer --worker-model auto --reference {FIX}/gen/verify/notes_ref.yaml --target {TMP}/vl_notes.yaml --spec "notes_ref に沿った YAML（.md と同じ最小契約）". Then classify these already-written samples (do not rewrite them): {FIX}/gen/verify/control_missing_key.json (syntactically valid JSON missing required_key), {FIX}/gen/verify/control_trunc.json (similar-length mid-truncation), {FIX}/gen/verify/control_fence.md (Markdown whose trailing fence is a legitimate code block). Run each verification and report status and the verification level (minimal|syntax|requirements) for each artifact. JSON parse-only is syntax + partial; Markdown/YAML minimal checks are minimal + partial; requirements only if acceptance keys were checked. For this evaluation, run a separate parent Bash verification for each artifact using exactly these commands: python3 {JUDGE_DIR}/flow_checks.py --verify syntax {TMP}/vl_config.json; python3 {JUDGE_DIR}/flow_checks.py --verify minimal {TMP}/vl_notes.md --expected-lines 30; python3 {JUDGE_DIR}/flow_checks.py --verify minimal {TMP}/vl_notes.yaml; python3 {JUDGE_DIR}/flow_checks.py --verify syntax {FIX}/gen/verify/control_missing_key.json; python3 {JUDGE_DIR}/flow_checks.py --verify syntax {FIX}/gen/verify/control_trunc.json; python3 {JUDGE_DIR}/flow_checks.py --verify minimal {FIX}/gen/verify/control_fence.md. These checks print only verification evidence, never artifact bodies. Report each filename followed by its verification level and status on its own line or Markdown table row. The truncated JSON must be reported failed/error or partial; the legitimate Markdown control must pass minimal checks and be reported minimal + partial. Do not claim requirements verification from these checks.

Using the token-shunt:bulk-reader skill (--worker-model auto), trace what happens after User creation across these 4 explicit paths: {FIX}/rails/app/models/user.rb {FIX}/rails/app/models/concerns/notifiable.rb {FIX}/rails/app/jobs/welcome_email_job.rb {FIX}/rails/app/mailers/user_mailer.rb --question "concern・job・mailer の名前と参照関係". First Agent must carry the first 3 paths; a later Agent the remaining path. Report the integrated answer with confirmed: items that name matching paths.

Use token-shunt:bulk-reader --worker-model auto on these four explicit paths: {FIX}/gen/collide/alpha.py {FIX}/rails/app/models/user.rb {FIX}/rails/app/models/concerns/notifiable.rb {FIX}/gen/collide/beta.py. First Agent must carry the first three paths and a later Agent the fourth. Question: does the TOKEN defined in alpha.py refer to the TOKEN in beta.py? Same-name symbols alone do not establish a reference. Integrate only matching reference evidence. If ambiguous, either perform at most one boundary confirmation with both files in one fresh Agent, or report the relationship as unconfirmed and status: partial. Do not infer a reference from a matching name.

Use token-shunt:bulk-reader (--worker-model auto) on {FIX}/gen/bulk_facts.py only --question "このファイルが呼ぶ外部サービスのホスト名". The answer requires a file that was not listed; the worker must report partial/unconfirmed rather than read other files. Report the worker's answer.

Use token-shunt:bulk-reader (--worker-model auto) on {FIX}/gen/bulk_facts.py --question "MAGIC_TOKEN の値".
